cards.explanation: The answer is the cities where He did most of His miracles. The text says Jesus began to denounce “…the cities in which most of His miracles had been performed, because they did not repent.” Those towns got the most to see. The text says the trouble was that they did not repent.

The answer is that they would have repented long ago. Jesus says that if those miracles had been performed in Tyre and Sidon, “…they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.” Tyre and Sidon were cities outside Israel. Notice He says long ago.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “But I tell you, it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than for you.” The “you” is Chorazin and Bethsaida, so it's Tyre and Sidon who get the more bearable day. It's a heavy line, friends, and Jesus doesn't water it down.

The answer is Hades. Jesus asks Capernaum, “…will you be lifted up to heaven? No, you will be brought down to Hades!” It's a hard word, and the question He asks first makes the drop even bigger. I think this one stings.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Sodom, it would have remained to this day.” Sodom is the city the LORD rained sulfur and fire on (Genesis 19:24). So the Lord of those miracles is saying Sodom would still be standing if it had seen what Capernaum saw.

The answer is little children. Jesus says, “I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children.” Good news for a stamper with no diploma, friends. The ones who receive it are little children.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “No one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him.” Knowing the Father comes through the Son. That's a big deal for every baker who wants to know God.
The answer is rest. Jesus says, “Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.” Notice He says all of you who are weary and burdened. Nobody is left off the list.

The answer is gentle and humble in heart. Jesus says, “…I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.” He describes His own heart. That's what you get, friends, when you come to Him and learn from Him.
The answer is easy and light. Jesus says, “For My yoke is easy and My burden is light.” Those are His words for what He asks us to carry. It's a good way to end His invitation.
